headline: A Bank of England deputy governor has warned that banks need fully separate backup systems in case AI-powered attackers get through their defences.
score_reason: Senior regulator warning with a concrete ask; it is guidance and speech, not a rule.
importance_line: Bank customers and the wider financial system depend on banks having independent backup systems, though the Bank of England is so far encouraging, not requiring, such plans.
summary: Reuters reports that Sarah Breeden, a deputy governor of the Bank of England, said on 15 October 2026 that banks can no longer assume their defences will hold against AI-enabled cyber attacks and should build 'bare metal' recovery options, meaning backup systems fully separate from their main technology. She also described AI advances as a systemic risk to global financial infrastructure.
